title: WiM / Calibration loop
description: The centrepiece: what the estimator believes, drawn on what was actually true. Estimate and truth come from TimescaleDB rather than Prometheus, because a replayed run pushes its plant state faster than any scrape interval and a gauge only keeps the last value scraped. Truth is absent in replay mode and the panels degrade to showing only the estimate, which is the correct behaviour for real data. Drift detectors, controller state and recalibration events arrive with the controller in phase 5; their panels are provisioned now and are empty until then, deliberately, so that the shape of the dashboard is fixed before the results are.

list.name: station
list.label: Station
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT station_id FROM wim.measurement_event ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Sensor gain: estimated vs true
panels.description: The headline. Both series are sensor-side -- sensor units per kg -- so neither has to be inverted in the query. The estimator fits in the prediction direction and reports through EstimatorState.sensor_gain; see calibration/base.py. A flat truth line with the estimate converging onto it is what a working loop looks like; a truth line that steps is an injected fault, and the interesting number is how long the estimate takes to follow it.

targets.rawSql: SELECT ts_start AS time, cal_gain AS "estimated gain" FROM wim.measurement_event WHERE $__timeFilter(ts_start) AND station_id IN ($station) ORDER BY 1
SELECT ts AS time, k_true AS "true gain" FROM truth.truth_timeseries WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND station_id IN ($station) ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Gain error
panels.description: Estimate minus truth, as a fraction of truth, at the most recent pass that has a truth point within a second of it. Nulls when the truth schema is empty, which is what replay mode looks like.

targets.rawSql: SELECT (e.cal_gain - t.k_true) / nullif(t.k_true, 0) AS "relative gain error" FROM wim.measurement_event e JOIN LATERAL (SELECT k_true FROM truth.truth_timeseries s WHERE s.station_id = e.station_id ORDER BY abs(extract(epoch FROM s.ts - e.ts_start)) LIMIT 1) t ON true WHERE $__timeFilter(e.ts_start) AND e.station_id IN ($station) ORDER BY e.ts_start DESC LIMIT 1

panels.title: Active profile
panels.description: The calibration every event in the window points at. More than one value here means a recalibration happened inside the window.

targets.rawSql: SELECT profile_id AS "profile", count(*) AS "events" FROM wim.measurement_event WHERE $__timeFilter(ts_start) AND station_id IN ($station) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Estimated bias (post zero-line residual)
panels.description: Deliberately NOT overlaid on q_true. The preprocessor's zero-line tracker removes the plant's zero line before the feature is taken, so what the estimator fits is the residual the tracker left behind -- order 1e-4 against a q_true of 0.05. Drawing them together would show a flat line and a near-zero line and read as a badly wrong estimator when it is a correct one. See calibration/base.py.

targets.rawSql: SELECT ts_start AS time, cal_bias AS "estimated bias" FROM wim.measurement_event WHERE $__timeFilter(ts_start) AND station_id IN ($station) ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Covariance trace
panels.description: Trace of the estimator state covariance: convergence made visible rather than argued. StaticAffine carries none, so this is empty until the Kalman estimator arrives in phase 5 -- which is the honest state of affairs, not a broken panel.

targets.rawSql: SELECT ts_start AS time, cal_covariance_trace AS "covariance trace" FROM wim.measurement_event WHERE $__timeFilter(ts_start) AND station_id IN ($station) AND cal_covariance_trace IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1

panels.title: True sensor temperature vs the probe
panels.description: The gap between them is what a temperature-compensating estimator is fighting: the probe has its own offset and noise, and compensating on the probe reading corrects for something slightly different from what actually happened.

targets.rawSql: SELECT ts AS time, t_sensor_true AS "true sensor" FROM truth.truth_timeseries WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND station_id IN ($station) ORDER BY 1
SELECT ts_start AS time, temperature_c AS "probe reading" FROM wim.measurement_event WHERE $__timeFilter(ts_start) AND station_id IN ($station) AND temperature_c IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Residual against the reference mass
panels.description: Estimate minus truth in kilograms, per pass. A residual stream centred on zero with no structure is a calibrated scale; a step is a fault, a ramp is drift, and a fan is a scale whose noise is growing.

targets.rawSql: SELECT e.ts_start AS time, e.mass_kg - t.true_mass_kg AS "residual" FROM wim.measurement_event e JOIN truth.truth_pass t ON t.station_id = e.station_id AND abs(extract(epoch FROM t.ts_peak - e.ts_peak)) < 0.25 WHERE $__timeFilter(e.ts_start) AND e.station_id IN ($station) ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Estimator updates
panels.description: How many reference observations the active state has folded in. A gauge, not a counter: it resets when a profile is replaced, and phase 5's adaptive estimators make it move continuously.

targets.rawSql: SELECT ts_start AS time, cal_update_count AS "updates" FROM wim.measurement_event WHERE $__timeFilter(ts_start) AND station_id IN ($station) ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Drift detector statistics
panels.description: One series per detector -- CUSUM, Page-Hinkley, ADWIN, KS -- read from Prometheus rather than the database, because a detector statistic is a property of the running controller and not of any stored event. Empty until phase 5.

panels.title: Controller state and recalibrations
panels.description: The MAPE-K state as a one-hot, with recalibrations as a rate beneath it. A loop that is recalibrating constantly is as broken as one that never does; both are visible here and nowhere else. Empty until phase 5.

panels.title: Profile version
panels.description: An activation ordinal, stepping once per profile change. A step function is what an annotation can be drawn against; a profile_id label here would open a new series per recalibration and hide the step it exists to show.
